subject: HealPath packaging: alignment, safe step-downs, and bundle carveouts
messages:
From: Chad Moreno <chad.moreno@healpath.com>

Cc: procurement@healpath.com
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Packaging questions: upgrade/downgrade safety nets and carveouts

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran the usage export against our pilot and have a few follow-ups around packaging before we move to procurement:

- How does Redwood handle a step-down (downgrade) if we drop below committed throughput mid-term? Is there a credit ladder or fixed proration?
- Can we carve out specific features (e.g., private model access + enhanced tracing) and keep a smaller base tier, or do add-ons force us into the next tier?
- If we enable prefix/KV caching across our tenant, does that change the eligible tier (throughput vs feature-bundling)?

Attached is our export and the rough monthly agg by route. We want a safe downgrade path for Q4 if traffic normalizes. Procurement asked for a concrete example (numbers) and an outline of SOW scope for a pilot extension.

Thanks,
Chad
Head of Platform Engineering
HealPath

Attachments: HealPath_current_usage_20250628.xlsx
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, procurement@healpath.com
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging questions: upgrade/downgrade safety nets and carveouts

Hi Chad —

Appreciate the upload. High-level answers up front, then I can schedule a walk-through with Ben (pricing/packaging) and Marissa (CS) to map to your contract language:

- Downgrade / step-down: we support a time-windowed step-down ladder with staged proration. Practically, customers can request one stepped downgrade per quarter with a lookback window (30 days) for committed throughput. We also offer a soft-credit buffer for first-time downgrades in a 12‑month rolling term.
- Feature carveouts: add-ons (private model hosting, enhanced tracing) can be attached to any base tier without forcing full tier migration; there is an effective minimum throughput threshold for some add-ons (we'll call these "tier gates") — we'll confirm exact numbers for HealPath.
- Caching impact: enabling prefix/KV caching reduces effective token compute and can shift recommended tier down by one bucket in some cases; we'll model that against your route mix.

Action items:
1) Ben will prepare a worked example with numbers and a downgrade ladder scenario (incl. credits).
2) Marissa will draft a short SOW for a 45-day pilot extension and a 2-hour packaging workshop.
3) Can you confirm preferred workshop dates next week (Wed/Thu AM PT)?

I'll loop Ben and Marissa in the next email.

Best,
Kim
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Chad / team —

Thanks, pulled the workbook and ran three illustrative scenarios. Summary below (I'll attach the sheet as well):

Scenario A — Conservative (keep current tier, soft credits)
- Keep current Reserved Tier (R2) for the term. First downgrade request within 12 months gets a 20% soft credit applied to next invoice, applied once. Proration uses daily usage cadence.
- Add-ons billed as linear per-seat/per-GPU rate; no forced tier migration.

Scenario B — Controlled step-down (one-step ladder)
- If traffic drops sustained >30 days below 70% of committed throughput, customer can step down one tier with 60-day notice. Billing: proration from next billing cycle + 10% step-down fee to cover reservation delta.

Scenario C — Cache-optimized (aggressive savings)
- If KV/prefix cache reduces effective token compute by >25% (measured over a 30-day rolling window), we recommend downgrading one tier without a step-down fee; credits capped at 25% of monthly invoice.

Worked example (from your numbers): if you move to R3 for pilot peak and then traffic normalizes to your baseline (sheet tab "Worked Examples") — net annual cost delta after credits is roughly -6% vs keeping R2, assuming caching improvements. Exacts in attached xlsx.

Attachment: Redwood_tier_stepdown_model_v1.xlsx (pricing ladder, formulas, worked examples). I'm including two contract-friendly bullets you can bring to procurement:
- We will state explicit downgrade gates (30-day lookback and one-step-per-quarter) in SOW to avoid mid-term churn.
- Any add-on that materially increases reserved capacity (private-hosted model variants) will be listed with a minimum throughput threshold in the SOW to prevent accidental tier escalation.

If this aligns, we'll bake the language into the SOW draft.
